newsitem.title: UK: Bakyrchik mulls share placing in near future.
newsitem.headline: Bakyrchik mulls share placing in near future.

text.p: Bakyrchik Gold Plc said on Wednesday it was considering a private placing of new shares to raise about $10 million to help fund three feasibility studies on production costs at the Bakyrchik gold mine in Kazakhstan.
Bakyrchik Gold, which reported a first-half loss of $16.4 million, said it would need substantially more money at a later stage if it eventually decided to develop the mine.
Preliminary results from the cost studies, which are already under way, indicate that production of one million tonnes a year would require a $220 million capital investment.
But the requirement would be significantly less if Bakyrchik opted for a lower production programme, Bakyrchik's managing director Roger Harris told Reuters.
The results of the feasability studies would be known in the next couple of months, Harris said.
Bakyrchik Gold in December agreed with the Kazakh government to raise its stake in the Bakyrchik mining joint venture to 85 percent from 40 percent at a cost of $65 million.
Of this sum, $45 million would have to raised in any second funding exercise for developing the mine.
Indochina Goldfields, the Canadian firm with mining financier Robert Friedman as its biggest shareholder, pledged to lend the remaining $20 million once the feasibility studies have been completed.
Indochina Goldfields, Bakyrchik Gold's largest shareholder with a 26.3 percent stake, will hold 15 percent in the Bakyrchik mining joint venture.
Bakyrchik said the Kazakh mining deposit was now estimated to have resources of 13.0 million ounces, up from a previous estimate of 10.5 million.
"We are a junior mining company with a hell of an asset and we are going to have to finance it: so yes, that's going to be a struggle," Harris said.
Bakyrchik shares were down four pence at 213 pence
